# Philosophy Quotes, Thinkers & Ideas | Verified & Sourced

> A sourced philosophy database: verified quotations traced to the work and passage they come from, indexed by thinker, work, concept, and theme — with the misattributions recorded.

A sourced philosophy database

## Philosophy Quotes, Thinkers & Ideas — Verified and Sourced

Every passage in this archive carries its source — thinker, work, and section — and every recorded line names the wording it came from. Where a quotation is commonly misattributed, the archive says so rather than repeating the popular byline.

[Trace a quotation to its source](https://www.philosophydef.com/quote-source) [Browse the archive](https://www.philosophydef.com/quotes)

696 sourced English passages by 146 thinkers across 62 traditions — 58 of them checked against the cited edition, 57 with the original wording recorded. From Plato and Confucius to Kwasi Wiredu, Nishida Kitarō, and Frantz Fanon. [How the levels work](https://www.philosophydef.com/about#verification-levels).

How to read

### Sourced first. Chance second.

The homepage withholds selection, and the archive refuses to withhold the citation. Every passage arrives with the work it comes from, so the encounter begins with the words and ends somewhere you can check.

Sourced

Each passage names the work, section, and edition it is cited from.

Checked

58 passages are checked against the cited edition; every page states its own level.

Chance

Each refresh draws another sourced passage from the corpus.

Attribution

### Who actually said it?

Paste any quotation into the [quote source finder](https://www.philosophydef.com/quote-source) to see the located record: the work and section, the wording in the original language, the forms that circulate in its place, and the lines most often attributed to the wrong author. Start with the [misattributed quotations](https://www.philosophydef.com/misattributed-quotes) the archive has already worked through, read how it [sources its texts](https://www.philosophydef.com/sourcing-method), or what it [publishes and corrects](https://www.philosophydef.com/editorial-policy).
